text:
Emma (support): FYI customer in ap-southeast-1 reporting ~20% of requests routed to hosted pool and intermittent 503s since ~04:40UTC. Dedicated pool shows all green. Also a sudden hosted billing surge on their account. Repro steps below. :warning:

Customer Ops: they pasted a sample request header that shows X-Route: hosted-forced even when tenant has a dedicated pin. sample request id: req-0a1b2c3d. Log snippet from their side: 

```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
x-request-id: req-0a1b2c3d
x-routing: hosted
```

Emma (support): their app observed increased latency (1200ms -> 2500ms) and occasional 503s when hosted endpoints picked up requests. They attached our control-plane request logs: 

```
route-service: decision=hosted fallback_reason=pin_ttl_miss tenant=acct-1234 pool=dedicated-ap-southeast-1
router: forwarded_to=hosted region=us-east-1
```

Nikhil (eng-oncall): looking. Can you confirm tenant id and a few full request-ids and the pinned pool id? Also did they recently change dedicated pool size or do a pool drain/maintenance?

Customer Ops: tenant acct-1234, pinned_pool: pool-apse-7, recent actions: autoscaler scaled pool down by 2 GPUs at 04:35UTC. Provided these request ids: req-0a1b2c3d, req-0f4e5d6c.

Sara (infra): quick hypothesis: pin TTL refresh race with autoscaler event -> router affinity table didn't get updated and considered pin stale, causing fallback to hosted. I'll pull router debug for those req ids.

Rick (billing): verified spike: customer saw ~130k extra hosted tokens between 04:35-05:10 UTC, billing lookup id bill-789. This matches their complaint. We need an immediate mitigation to stop further hosted spillover.

Nikhil (eng-oncall): mitigation plan 1) temporarily increase preferential routing TTL on routers for pinned tenants to 120s to avoid transient misses 2) disable aggressive fallback to hosted for tenants with active recent pin state 3) create alert on pin.miss.rate > 0.5% so support/eng oncall get paged. I'll open an emergency rollout.

route-bot: Deploy started: config/router-pin-guard v1.1 -> canary on routers in ap-southeast-1

Emma (support): repro steps the customer used (works locally for us when we simulate drain):
1) create dedicated pin via dashboard (tenant acct-1234 -> pool-apse-7)
2) scale pool down by 2 GPUs quickly (simulate autoscaler)
3) fire continuous requests: 
```
for i in $(seq 1 200); do 
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "X-Tenant: acct-1234" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' -o /dev/null &
done
```
Observe logs: many requests show route-service decision=hosted immediately after scale event.

Sara (infra): got router logs for req-0a1b2c3d: 
```
[04:36:02] router: lookup_pin tenant=acct-1234 -> cache_miss
[04:36:02] router: evaluate_fallback -> hosted (reason: pin_ttl_expired)
[04:36:02] router: forwarded_to hosted-us-east-1
```
This looks like the pin TTL was not refreshed atomically when the autoscaler updated pool metadata. The control plane's pin-refresh job is eventual and can lose a small window during concurrent pool updates.

Nikhil (eng-oncall): root cause summary: pin refresh race during pool resize leading to transient cache misses on the router -> fallback to hosted. Two contributing factors: a) TTL refresh frequency too low; b) router cache treats cache_miss as immediate fallback rather than conservative retry when control-plane reports recent pin change.

Nikhil (eng-oncall): short-term fixes pushed: 
- increase pin refresh frequency from 30s -> 10s for pool change events
- change router fallback policy: on cache_miss check control-plane quick lookup for last-modified timestamp (within 60s) before forcing hosted route
- add metric pin.cache_miss and alerting

route-bot: Deploy succeeded: config/router-pin-guard v1.1 -> canary complete, rolling to region ap-southeast-1

Rick (billing): I put a temporary credit hold on billed hosted overage for acct-1234 while we investigate — will coordinate with finance.

Emma (support): I'll send a note to the customer with the mitigation and ask for verification. Please add this to the postmortem queue if the billing impact > $1000.

Sara (infra): follow-up tickets: INF-4523 add stronger reconciler run on pool metadata change, INF-4524 router conservative fallback, INF-4525 metrics+alerts.

Emma (support): Thanks team. Customer asked for ETA on permanent fix — can we aim for next week for reconciler + router policy change?

Nikhil (eng-oncall): aiming for next-week delivery. Will update this thread when reconciler PR lands and when billing follow-up complete. :thumbsup:
